entry.title: Toward space-optimal approximate colored indexes at scale. Searching current petabase-scale sequence repositories requires indexes that combine compact storage with high query throughput.
entry.summary:
Searching current petabase-scale sequence repositories requires indexes that combine compact storage with high query throughput. Although exact colored indexes retain complete sequence information, their construction and storage costs can become substantial for highly diverse collections. Indexes based on approximate membership query (AMQ) filters offer a compact alternative with fast construction and queries.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #rust #infosec

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Non-Interactive Threshold Mercurial Signatures with Applications to Threshold DAC
entry.summary:
In a mercurial signature, a signer signs a representative $m$ of an equivalence class of messages on behalf of a representative $\mathsf{pk}$ of an equivalence class of public keys, receiving the signature $\sigma$. One can then transform $\sigma$ into a signature $\sigma'$ on an equivalent (to $m$) message $m'$ under an equivalent (to $\mathsf{pk}$) public key $\mathsf{pk}'$. Mercurial signatures are helpful in constructing delegatable anonymous credentials (DACs): their privacy properties enable straightforward randomization of a credential chain, hiding the identity of each signer while preserving the authenticity of the overall credential.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust

entry.title: Financial Advisors and Retirees' Risk-taking -- by Allison T. Cole, Maarten Meeuwis, Alessandro Previtero, Noah Stoffman
entry.summary:
Advised retirees keep about two-thirds of their portfolios in equities well into old age—30 to 40 percentage points more than non-advised retirees, target-date funds, or common rules of thumb. These allocations reflect active choices rather than inertia, and they adjust gradually toward a new advisor’s investment style following advisor switches. Equity shares rise with relationship tenure, and advisor influence is strongest among clients with low financial knowledge or risk tolerance, consistent with trust facilitating risk-taking.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #rust
